text: This extract tells three stories about a figure named Áed. One Áed dwelled in a lovely yet lifeless place. He fled that place and traveled to Saint Patrick. Patrick released him from the remaining hold of Fairyland. The escape agrees with Irish fairy-lover tradition. The Saint Patrick close seems to be a later Christian change. A second Áed was the son of Lir. He was one of the enchanted children of Lir. A jealous stepmother changed him into a swan. The change lasted nine hundred years. The third Áed sat on the throne of Tara. He ruled as king in the sixth century. He trusted a magic cow to keep him safe in battle. He left the cow at home before the fight. He fell in that fight.

okr.objective: The fairy (other Celtic) fragment gives three stories of Áed.
key_results: An Áed fled a barren fairy land and sought out Saint Patrick.
Áed, son of Lir, spent nine hundred years as a swan.
Áed, king of Tara, trusted a magic cow he left behind.
He died in the war he entered without the cow.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
